_readme: Copy this file to data/config.json and fill in your values. Every key is optional: an absent or empty value leaves its feature dormant. Keys prefixed with an underscore are explanations. This file is generated from server/settingschema.py (python -m server.settingschema example --write); edit the table, not the file. data/ is git-ignored, so nothing in your copy reaches the repo.
_you: You: Who Vira works for, and when.
_owner_name: Used in the cockpit greeting and the daily-brief narrative.
_assistant_timezone: An IANA zone such as America/New_York. Empty uses this computer's local time. Quiet hours, deadlines, the admin inbox and calendar planning all read it.
_assistant_kids_names: Comma-separated. A calendar proposal naming one of them files under the kids calendar when the model states no lane.
_assistant: Assistant: The background worker that reads new messages for commitments and keeps reminders current.
_assistant_enabled: Scans new texts and mail for commitments and deadlines, keeps the reminders list current, and reconciles recent indexed messages after downtime. Every other assistant setting depends on it.
_assistant_catchup_days: How far back the first scan looks in the message index.
_assistant_debounce_s: Wait this long after a message before processing it, so a conversation in progress is read once.
_assistant_batch_size: How many contacts one background pass processes.
_coverage_enabled: Uses the routine in the Childcare window: a caregiver cancelling in iMessage, a half day, or a closure on a day nobody covers puts a pickup block on the calendar and asks you once who is taking it. Needs the assistant running.
_coverage_calendar_blocks: Off keeps each block as a suggestion in Attention instead. Blocks go on the family calendar and never invite anyone.
_coverage_block_minutes: A child's own block length in the routine overrides this.
_notifications: Notifications: The iMessage channel Vira texts you on, and which features may use it.
_notify_enabled: The channel every alert uses. Off silences all of them.
_notify_handle: Your own self-thread number, e.g. +12125551234. Empty leaves every notification dormant.
_notify_tier: Inbound email from a contact at this tier (profile or master tier) pings you. Throttled to one per sender per 6 hours and 20 a day.
_assistant_notify: Overdue and due-soon reminders. Respects quiet hours and the daily cap.
_ai_health_notify: A green-to-red edge and the recovery. Dormant unless a handle is set.
_subs_notify_threshold_usd: Text when a renewal is within 7 days and the per-cycle amount clears this. Annual renewals always ping. Deduped per merchant and date.
_imessage_reply_enabled: Vira acts on reversible in-app things immediately and confirms once before anything that leaves this machine (server/inbound.py). Dormant unless a handle is set.
_inbound_ignore_prefixes: Prefixes of machine-sent texts that also land in the self-thread and must never be read as you talking. Vira's own sends are already covered by the "Vira: " prefix and the send ledger.
_sms_fallback: For Android or iMessage-less recipients. Needs Text Message Forwarding to the paired iPhone so Messages owns an SMS account. A contact can also be marked SMS on their person page.
_send_verify_seconds: How long Vira watches chat.db for an iMessage delivery error before giving up. 0 disables the reactive check.
_calendar: Calendar: Where the assistant files events and the hours it plans around.
_assistant_calendar_name: Chosen with the calendar picker in Config > Calendar.
_assistant_calendar_kids_name: School, classes, playdates and childcare that never need you, filed for your information. Falls back to the personal calendar.
_assistant_calendar_family_name: Family plans, parent evenings, RSVP'd or not. Falls back to the personal calendar.
_assistant_calendar_block_minutes: Vira reserves free personal work time before a task's deadline in blocks this long, inside the work hours above.
_assistant_calendar_auto_create: Otherwise every proposed event waits for your approval in Attention.
_appointment_calendar_entries: A doctor's or service's reminder (an SMS short code, a booking site, a patient portal) that states a date and time becomes one event on the personal calendar, however many reminders repeat it. Nobody is invited. Off keeps each as a suggestion in Attention. Needs the assistant running; the brief shows them either way.
_appointment_travel_minutes: Shown in the brief as a leave-by time and kept free when Vira plans work blocks. Video and phone visits get none. 0 turns it off.
_family_calendars: Calendar names as they appear in Calendar.app, tagged as family in the daily brief, e.g. ["Family", "Kids"].
_brief_remote_events: Event-title substrings (case-insensitive) treated as remote or virtual in the daily brief, e.g. ["Weekly Standup"]. A remote event is never flagged as an overlap against a same-time in-person event (two remote events still conflict). Microsoft 365 events also auto-detect via the Graph isOnlineMeeting flag.
_mail: Mail: Mail accounts and the email index.
_graph_email: The account the Connect M365 button and the cockpit banner use.
_mail_body_index: Puts every email, including ones you sent, into the searchable message index that Find and the assistant read. Off means the index holds texts only. The background sweep indexes 100 messages every 3 minutes; the one-time history walk is `python -m server.textindex backfill mail --full`.
_msgraph_client_id: Config > Mail > Microsoft 365 starts recovery or sign-in automatically and fills this in. Browser login needs a Mobile and desktop redirect http://localhost/api/mail/graph/browser/callback and delegated User.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send and Calendars.Read. Enable public client flows for device login.
_msgraph_tenant: The tenant id or domain of the app registration; filled in by the Microsoft 365 setup.
_contacts: Contacts: Contact storage and who may update profiles.
_crm_root: Directory holding people.json, optional master.json and profiles/. Config > Contacts > Contact storage (advanced) validates an existing CRM or selects a fresh import destination. Connecting preserves person IDs and files; switching an established CRM requires compatible identities. Until people.json exists there, Vira boots in fixture mode with one demo contact (Vira themself).
_self_record: The folder holding canon/MASTER_HISTORY.md (career evidence), your resume and application work. Connect it in Config > Contacts > Contact storage (advanced) > Career record storage. Connecting does not grant Brain or model access. Empty = <crm_root>/self.
_assistant_contact_updates: Adds durable facts and refreshes the relationship summary on People cards as conversations happen. Off keeps the assistant to commitments only. Does nothing while the assistant is off.
_apple_contacts_push: macOS only. Company, title, birthday, location, email and phone order and labels, the relationship, the when-we-met date, profile links and the Vira notes block sync to the phone.
_contacts_sync: macOS only. A background pass brings new phone contacts and new handles into the CRM, fills empty card fields from the phone, and keeps the Sync tab's report current. Nothing is deleted on either side; a card that had content on both sides is kept whole and flagged for you to read.
_contacts_sync_push_auto: On: every pass also writes CRM changes to the matched Apple cards. Off: changes wait in People > Sync until you press Push.
_contacts_sync_interval: How often the background pass runs.
_brain: Brain: Vaults, Reader folders, and what each one exposes.
_vault_root: Notes vault the Brain window indexes (Obsidian or any folder of markdown; FTS plus local nomic embeddings via Ollama; nothing leaves the machine at index time). Set it from Config > Brain. Empty = the Brain stays dormant.
_vault_sources: Each entry has stable id, name, root and optional dirs, read_enabled, write_enabled, model_exposure, model_exclude_dirs, exclude_dirs, purpose, contexts, capture_dir, write_scope, write_dirs, protected_dirs, allow_publish. Edited per vault in Config > Brain.
_vault_primary: Policy and name overrides for the primary vault, using the same fields as vault_sources. Empty preserves legacy single-vault read/write behavior. The plan rendering hook is off unless allow_publish is true.
_vault_default_destination: Stable source id for otherwise unqualified saves. Explicit destinations and context routes take precedence. Empty asks when more than one vault is writable.
_vault_dirs: Vault subdirectories to index (recursive), plus root-level .md files always. Empty = the default set (wiki, Briefs, Sessions, retros, brain-retros).
_vault_exclude_dirs: Directory NAMES skipped at any depth in every connected vault, on top of qocha's own defaults (.git, .obsidian, .venv). Each vault's own "Folders never indexed" list in Config > Brain is the per-vault version; this one applies everywhere.
_library_machine_dirs: Library: which folders of each vault are machine output (generated reports, session logs, bulk captures), hidden from the subject map until shown. Keyed by vault id; each entry is a vault-relative folder, or "!folder" to keep a folder inside a machine folder as knowledge. Edited per vault in Config > Brain and from the Library map.
_atlas_vaults: Extra Image Atlas vaults as [{id, name, root}]; the primary vault is always included. Toggled per vault in Config > Brain.
_reader_sources: Folders outside Vira connected to the Reader, as [{path, kind, glob, label}]. Each is read and never written or copied. kind is dossier | plan | retro | brief | walkthrough; glob is a filename pattern inside the folder (default *.html). Edited in Config > Brain > Reader document folders.
_answer_source_policy: Per-kind overrides for what the answering model may read: {kind: {read_enabled, model_exposure}}. Empty allows every approved source.
_ai: AI: Providers, models, and app-wide model defaults.
_ai_provider: anthropic | openai | google | xai. Chosen from the provider cards in Config > AI.
_ai_backend: "cli" uses the provider's local CLI login (a subscription); "api" uses an API key from the environment variable named below.
_cli_model: An ALIAS the CLI resolves to the newest model of that tier: sonnet | opus | haiku | fable. Never a full model id; an id here names a generation and starts lying the week the next one ships.
_api_model: Empty = let Vira pick, at call time, the newest model of the cli_model tier from the list your API key can reach. Set a full id only to pin one deliberately.
_openai_cli_model: Empty runs whatever ~/.codex/config.toml is set to.
_xai_cli_model: The model the Grok Build CLI runs on your Grok subscription. Empty runs the CLI's own default (the one `grok models` marks).
_model_roster: The model ids enabled for pickers across every provider. Empty means everything the catalog offers, so a future model arrives enabled unless you have curated. Edited in Config > Advanced AI settings.
_providers_disabled: Provider ids (anthropic | openai | google | xai) that are never drafted on and never run a session: a dispatch pinned to one, a go-to set to one, and the drafting ladder all REFUSE by name instead of rerouting. Toggle per provider under Config > AI.
_module_models: {module id: {provider, backend, model}} chosen with the model picker beside a module's work. Empty rows inherit the defaults above.
_chat_model: The model its session runs on. Empty = the session default (cli_model), which is what every other owner session uses.
_judge_model: Model for fresh-eyes judge sessions (circuit judge stages and the Judge button on job history). Accepts sonnet | opus | haiku | fable.
_chat_effort: Passed to the chat session as its effort level when set. Empty = the model's default.
_model_alias_overrides: Corrections for aliases this machine's CLI resolves WRONG, e.g. {"opus": "claude-opus-5"} when --model opus still gives an older generation. Re-measure after a CLI upgrade with: claude --print --output-format json --model opus 'Say OK.' (read modelUsage) and DELETE the entry once the alias is correct again.
_api_key_env: The environment variable holding the Anthropic API key when the backend is "api".
_dossier_cost_estimate_usd: Shown beside the profile build button as a spend estimate.
_workers: Background work: Sweeps and watchers that run on a cadence.
_ai_health_enabled: Deterministic AI-backend health watcher: probes `claude auth status` (or the API key) on a cadence so an expired login surfaces out-of-band instead of as a silently dead cockpit job. Uses none of the model. The /api/health/ai probe still works on demand when this is off.
_ai_health_interval_min: Clamped to a 60 second floor. The probe is cheap and spends no tokens.
_source_health_enabled: The source-health sentinel (server/sourcehealth.py) learns a baseline per source (calendar events per weekday, mail and iMessage arrivals, vault notes and search hits). When one falls to zero against it, the brief and every tool answer from that source say it looks broken, and one fix-it item is filed in the ideas backlog. No model call.
_source_health_interval_min: Each check is a few COUNT queries plus the M365 calendar read the brief already makes.
_media_archive_enabled: macOS treats ~/Library/Messages/Attachments as an evictable cache: Messages in iCloud offloads the bytes under storage pressure and leaves the chat.db row, so without this a conversation's media history decays into a list of filenames.
_media_archive_root: Empty = data/media-archive. Point it at an external volume to keep it off the boot disk, whose fullness is what triggers the eviction.
_media_archive_max_gb: 0 = no cap. A reached cap is reported in the sweep log and in the status payload, never silently applied.
_media_archive_interval_min: Each pass only has to copy what macOS has downloaded since the last one.
_mail_archive_enabled: The raw message as the provider holds it, attachments inside, one .eml per message. Without it mail lives only on the provider: the text index keeps a stripped body and the attachment index the files it chose, and neither gives a message back.
_mail_archive_root: Empty = data/mail-archive. Point it at an external volume to keep a large mailbox off the boot disk.
_mail_archive_max_gb: 0 = no cap. A reached cap is reported in the sweep log and in the status payload, never silently applied.
_mail_archive_interval_min: Each pass takes what arrived since the last one, then walks the history newest first, 200 messages per account at most. The text index and the attachment index read the archive's files for the accounts it covers, so new mail is held, searchable and its attachments indexed within minutes; the history is the CLI backfill's job.
_mail_archive_workers: IMAP connections walking the history at once when the CLI backfill runs; the background sweep uses one. One message per round trip per connection is the rate. Gmail allows 15 per account, shared with your mail apps; a walker refused at the limit steps aside, and the backfill retries with fewer.
_receipts_sweep_days: The receipts pass sweeps mailboxes and indexed attachments for invoice and receipt evidence, flagged merchants first. Dormant until a mail account is configured. On demand per merchant from its card.
_mercury_poll_hours: How often Subscriptions polls Mercury for new charges. Connect a Read Only token in Config > Banking. Dormant until connected.
_boards_auto_score: After each sweep (and every few minutes between) the poller dispatches ONE scoring session at a time over the unscored backlog, 40 roles per session, gated on an AI actually being connected. Off restores the manual Score-new button in the Applications boards strip.
_boards_auto_rescore: Once nothing is unscored, drain the stale backlog the same way: roles whose analysis predates your record's last change get re-judged, one session at a time, tier-first then oldest. Real spend on a large backlog; off leaves the per-role Rescore button as the only path.
_idea_tag_interval_min: Each tick embeds any new ideas locally and makes at most ONE model call, so a fresh backlog tags itself over an hour rather than in one spend.
_doc_tag_interval_min: Each tick tags at most ONE batch of 12, so a fresh library groups itself over an hour or two and nothing waits on it.
_doc_thumb_interval_min: Dormant without a Chrome, Chromium or Edge on the machine; the browser path below overrides the probe.
_circle_refresh_min: Re-matches the Visual Network's social circles to their stable identities and re-reads (one model call each, at most four per pass) only the circles whose members or shared group chats changed.
_sessions: Agent sessions: Live coding sessions Vira dispatches.
_session_default_mode: manual pauses every risky tool call for your Approve/Deny; acceptEdits lets file edits land but asks before commands; bypassPermissions runs everything. The containment is structural: a writing session is placed in its own worktree and the gate refuses any write aimed at the live checkout. Per-run override in the UI.
_session_max_live: Each holds a CLI subprocess against the plan. Launches past the cap are refused with a clear error. Sessions parked in their reply window do not count.
_session_auto_allow: Read-only tools the permission gate approves on its own. Anything else that reaches the gate raises an Approve/Deny card.
_session_permission_timeout: The session then continues rather than hanging forever.
_session_reply_window_hours: Status "waiting on your reply", compose bar live, before it finalizes on its own. Ending it with Finish is the normal path; this is only the safety reap.
_session_landing_card: Vira itself raises the merge / try it first / keep playing / discard decision card (in the terminal, the Attention window, and on your phone) instead of leaving that question in the transcript. Try it first serves a fresh, local-only instance of the branch and brings the card back with its link; it is never bridged to the tailnet automatically. Off leaves the session to end however it ends.
_session_branch_first: The gate refuses writes to the live checkout; the result is always merged or thrown away with the branch.
_session_max_buffer_mb: The SDK bounds one NDJSON line; 1 MiB killed three sessions that ran Edit on static/app.js. Bounded, not removed, so a runaway CLI cannot exhaust the runner.
_atlas_anchor_org: Company name pinned as the Contact Atlas anchor cluster (substring-matched against CRM company fields). Empty = no pinned cluster; communities still form by label propagation.
_atlas_max_nodes: The N most-active tiered contacts rendered in the graph. Keeps the mesh legible and the edge passes cheap.
_atlas_min_edge_weight: Edges whose fused multi-signal weight falls below this are dropped.
_channels: Phone and WhatsApp: The phone companion and the WhatsApp sidecar.
_companion_hub_url: URL the Android companion pairing QR points the phone at, e.g. http://your-machine.your-tailnet.ts.net:8377. Empty = auto-detect: the Tailscale MagicDNS name, then the tailnet IP, then the LAN IP.
_whatsapp_bridge_port: Linked-device sidecar, 127.0.0.1 only. Config > WhatsApp > Connect prepares pinned packages and shows the pairing QR; needs Node.js 20 or newer with npm. Dormant until paired.
_whatsapp_node_bin: PATH name or absolute path of the node binary the sidecar runs on.
_career: Applications: Career record, job boards, and eligibility.
_applications_universe: Where the scored candidate universe lives (candidate-universe/role/*.json plus *-raw-scores.json). Written by the front door. Empty = <self_record>/analysis.
_applications_packages_root: One generated package per application (resume, cover letter, interview materials). Empty = ~/Documents/CV/15-applications when that folder exists, otherwise <self_record>/15-applications.
_applications_locations: Place names you will work in, e.g. ["Berlin", "BER"]. Empty means unfiltered unless another location setting is configured. Eligibility gates the phone ping and the default view, never what gets fetched.
_applications_remote_regions: Territories from which you can accept region-limited remote work, e.g. ["Germany", "Central European Time"]. Private preference data; empty means Vira does not infer territories from your offices.
_applications_remote_exclude: A private regex or list of remote-location labels that are outside your search. Empty excludes no geography.
_applications_region_hints: A private regex or list used when a posting mixes Remote with several locations. Empty accepts no geography by product default.
_applications_boards: Replaces the board registry file with an inline list. Normally unset; boards are registered from the Applications front door.
_applications_sources: [{slug, company, path}] explorer directories (each with a data.js) ingested as static role corpora instead of the lab root.
_applications_connections_csv: A LinkedIn-style connections export used for warm-path lookups. Empty = <self_record>/connections.csv when present.
_lab_root: Local checkout holding careers-teardown explorer directories to ingest as STATIC role corpora. Optional: the Applications module's normal source is the live board poller.
_pivot_keywords: Extra words widening the Radar "Reconnect - pivot" fingerprint. The target companies and lanes are always derived live from the Applications universe.
_lessons: Lessons and review: The corrections ledger and review queue.
_evidence_retro_dir: Directory the Evidence Ledger mines session retros from (glob "* vira.md"). Empty = ~/TC-IL/Sessions. The ledger also reads this checkout's own git-ignored retros/*.md when present.
_lessons_ledger_path: The ledger the lesson-recurrence counter reads (Work > RECORD > Rules). Empty = ~/.claude/LESSONS.md; a missing file leaves the module dormant. Vira only ever READS this file.
_lessons_state_dir: results/<day>/*.json session digests plus lessons-proposed.jsonl and lessons-decided.jsonl. Empty = ~/.claude/sessions.
_lessons_retro_dirs: Retro directories the counter reads as the markdown fallback, ALL projects. Empty = the retro folder above (or its default) plus this checkout's retros/.
_lessons_script_path: The corrections-ledger CLI the review queue shells out to; it owns every ledger write. Empty = ~/.claude/scripts/lessons.py.
_lesson_promote_at: Distinct sessions that must describe breaking a tier-2 rule before the counter stages a promotion proposal (a proposed idea in the Queue, never a ledger write).
_lesson_candidates_per_rule: Rung-2 cost ceiling, newest first; drops are counted in the run record, never silent.
_review_inbox_dir: Surfaced in the review queue. Empty = <self_record>/inbox/notes.
_review_history_path: Read for open adjudication flags and questions. Empty = <self_record>/canon/MASTER_HISTORY.md.
_intake: Intake: Filing messages into vault folders.
_correspondence: {enabled, auto_file, model_classification, auto_confidence, catchup_days, routes}. Edited in Attention > Inbox; routes name a vault and a category.
_system: System: Service names, runtime limits, and external tools.
_fixture_mode: true/false forces demo/real mode; null (the default) auto-detects: fixture when the contact folder has no people.json.
_launchd_label: If Vira runs as a launchd service, its label (e.g. com.example.vira). The in-app updater then restarts via launchctl kickstart; empty = the updater refuses web-triggered restarts.
_windows_task_name: The task that keeps Vira running (scripts\run.ps1 -Register creates it, default name "Vira", and records it here). Empty = the updater refuses web-triggered restarts on Windows.
_keychain_prefix: Prefixes every Keychain service name so a second instance on the same Mac cannot read or overwrite the live instance's secrets. Empty keeps the historical names. VIRA_KEYCHAIN_PREFIX in the environment wins.
_cpu_slots: How many CPU-heavy requests may run at once before the rest wait.
_loop_stall_threshold_s: Lag past which the watchdog counts the loop as stalled. Empty = 2.
_thumb_browser: Explicit browser binary; empty = probe PATH and app bundles.
_ytdlp_path: Used by the reading-room full ingest to stage YouTube caption transcripts into the vault. Empty = probe PATH; an absent binary reports "yt-dlp not installed" and articles still stage.
_site_root: Checkout of the owner's public site repo. Used by the sitedocs migration and the blog publish pipeline. Empty = both stay dormant.
_design_foundation_root: The design-system repo the Design studio edits; missing = dormant.
